correctness.rationale: The normalized Gabor system at area 1/2 reduces by Zak/Parseval to absence of a pair of Zak zeros. The parity Wronskian identity follows by absolutely convergent double-sum regrouping; its coefficient C_lambda is positive for all lambda>0 using Poisson summation and Jacobi product monotonicity. The Gaussian Zak factor has exactly the known half-half torus zeros. Those are incompatible with nonzero affine constant term; the odd endpoint has a direct zero. The proof covers complex coefficients, all positive aspect ratios and the Gaussian endpoint. Standalone numerical checks confirm nontrivial identities but do not replace the analytic steps.

value.rationale: The first-Hermite frame set has an arithmetic failure at area 1/2. Classifying every complex mixture with the Gaussian at exactly this forbidden lattice, uniformly over all aspect ratios, is a natural missing boundary problem. The result shows that the nonframe phenomenon is confined to one projective direction in the two-dimensional Hermite span, and gives the exact analytic obstruction-removal mechanism. This is a natural structural frame-set theorem, not a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary finite table.
